adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — The Integration.DoesNotExist branch calls pipeline.next_step() without verifying installation ownership, allowing an authenticated attacker to submit another user's installation ID and bypass the ownership check before the webhook creates the integration row.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue. Looking at the diff, when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught at line 481, the code calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without any ownership verification. The ownership check (comparing github_authenticated_user to integration.metadata['sender']['login']) only happens AFTER the try/except block when the integration already exists. This means if an attacker submits an installation_id before the webhook creates the Integration row, they bypass the ownership verification entirely. The OAuth flow authenticates the user but doesn't prevent them from claiming any installation_id that doesn't yet have an Integration record.
